title: Tennis Showcase
headline_insight: A time-decayed in-game prior transfers cleanly across tours: fit on WTA and tested on ATP, held-out Brier improves from 0.155 to 0.1432 (delta 0.01184), verdict REPLICATED, while a surface-specific hold prior is REJECTED.
what_it_means: The base (state, time) model, fit on one tour and tested leak-free on the other, is beaten by adding the prior in both directions, calibration only, no market claim. But making the hold prior surface-specific does not help: the pooled Brier change is only +0.000121 on ATP and +0.002492 on WTA, so the planted null dies.
how_to_read: Two preregistered gate receipts, the cross-corpus pregame prior (lower held-out Brier is better) and the in-game surface-context layer (H1 surface-specific versus H0 surface-blind).
why_it_matters: It shows a genuine cross-corpus calibration win sitting next to an honest reject, the gate catches both rather than only the wins.
caveat: CALIBRATION only (held-out Brier / Diebold-Mariano), never a market edge or dollar claim. Tennis has a served live model but no in-game grade corpus locally, so this surfaces the two receipts that exist, not a recomputed in-game summary.
as_of: gate_tennis.json + surface_hold_verdict.json receipts (no generation timestamp in artifact)
